items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1960-06-15
items.q: I started playing with René Parker... They made up a band... I got with that band. It was called Onida Jazz Band.

ctx.x: Very well. There, it's going again the machine stopped for a second. We were talking about Celestan and can you think of anything else that you went on from there after that group? After that group?

Well, I started playing with René Parker, a trumpet player. A fella, him and Big Fire, they call him, trombone player. They made up a band and they was going down the country, the Burris and all down in St. Bernard Parish. Mostly, that's the most of their work were down there playing. So, I got with that band. It was called Onida Jazz Band. And I drifted right along with them playing. I must have stayed with them about two years. The job was pretty good. And I did alright with them. And then I came back and…
Yeah, we're having trouble with this recorder now, but we'll try to finish up quickly so we'll get the rest of your life in here within five minutes if we can.
